primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Loss of functional dystrophin destabilizes the sarcolemma during contraction, causing repeated muscle-fiber injury, necrosis, and progressive replacement by fat and connective tissue.
vignette: A 5-year-old boy has difficulty running and climbing stairs. He uses his hands to push himself upright from the floor and has enlarged calves. Serum creatine kinase is markedly elevated.
lead: Loss of which protein most directly causes this disorder?
distractor_notes: Fibrillin-1 defects cause Marfan syndrome, not progressive childhood muscular dystrophy.
Type IV collagen defects are associated with Alport syndrome and basement-membrane abnormalities.
Spectrin defects can cause hereditary spherocytosis rather than proximal skeletal-muscle weakness.
Merlin is the NF2 tumor suppressor and is unrelated to sarcolemmal stability.
key_expl: Duchenne muscular dystrophy results from DMD variants that abolish functional dystrophin, a protein required for muscle-membrane stability during contraction.
objective: Connect Gowers sign, calf pseudohypertrophy, and high creatine kinase with loss of dystrophin in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
clues: markedly elevated creatine kinase in a young boy

sources.title: Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophy
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes dystrophin deficiency as the cause of Duchenne muscular dystrophy and progressive skeletal and cardiac muscle injury.

sources.title: DMD gene
sources.support: The DMD gene encodes dystrophin, which helps stabilize and protect muscle fibers during contraction.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: FBN1 loss disrupts fibrillin-1 microfibrils and dysregulates transforming growth factor-beta signaling, weakening elastic connective tissues including the ascending aorta.
vignette: A 17-year-old boy is tall with long extremities and fingers. He has superior lens displacement and dilation of the aortic root.
lead: Which protein is most likely abnormal?
distractor_notes: Type I collagen abnormalities cause osteogenesis imperfecta and some Ehlers-Danlos phenotypes rather than classic Marfan syndrome.
Type IV collagen abnormalities cause Alport syndrome.
Dystrophin deficiency causes Duchenne or Becker muscular dystrophy.
Elastase is a protease; Marfan syndrome results from an extracellular microfibril protein defect, not excess elastase as the primary inherited lesion.
key_expl: Marfan syndrome is caused by pathogenic variants in FBN1, which encodes fibrillin-1.
objective: Associate the skeletal, ocular, and aortic manifestations of Marfan syndrome with fibrillin-1 deficiency.

sources.title: Marfan syndrome
sources.support: NIAMS describes Marfan syndrome as a connective-tissue disorder due to FBN1 abnormalities affecting skeleton, eyes, and aorta.

sources.title: FBN1 gene
sources.support: FBN1 encodes fibrillin-1, a major component of extracellular microfibrils.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Quantitative or structural defects in type I collagen weaken bone matrix and can also affect sclerae, dentin, and hearing structures.
vignette: A 7-year-old girl has had four fractures after minor trauma. Examination shows blue sclerae and mild hearing loss. Her father had recurrent childhood fractures.
lead: Which diagnosis best explains these findings?
distractors: Rickets due to vitamin D deficiency
distractor_notes: Achondroplasia causes disproportionate short stature from impaired endochondral ossification, not fragile bones with blue sclerae.
Rickets causes defective mineralization, bone pain, and deformity but does not usually produce a dominant family history with blue sclerae.
Osteopetrosis causes abnormally dense but brittle bones due to defective osteoclast function and lacks the classic blue sclerae pattern.
Marfan syndrome causes tall stature, ectopia lentis, and aortic disease rather than recurrent childhood fractures from type I collagen defects.
key_expl: Recurrent low-trauma fractures, blue sclerae, hearing involvement, and an autosomal dominant family history are classic for osteogenesis imperfecta.
objective: Recognize osteogenesis imperfecta from bone fragility plus extra-skeletal manifestations of type I collagen disease.

sources.title: Osteogenesis imperfecta
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes osteogenesis imperfecta as a collagen-related bone fragility disorder with recurrent fractures, blue sclerae, and hearing loss.

sources.title: COL1A1 gene
sources.support: COL1A1 encodes a major component of type I collagen and pathogenic variants commonly cause osteogenesis imperfecta.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Type V collagen defects impair collagen fibril organization, producing hyperextensible fragile skin, widened atrophic scars, easy bruising, and generalized joint hypermobility.
vignette: A 20-year-old woman has markedly hyperextensible skin, generalized joint hypermobility, easy bruising, and widened atrophic scars.
lead: Pathogenic variants in which collagen gene are commonly responsible for the classical form of this disorder?
distractor_notes: COL4A5 variants cause X-linked Alport syndrome.
COL1A1 variants commonly cause osteogenesis imperfecta and some other connective-tissue disorders, but classical EDS is strongly associated with type V collagen genes.
FBN1 encodes fibrillin-1 and causes Marfan syndrome when mutated.
DMD encodes dystrophin and causes Duchenne or Becker muscular dystrophy.
key_expl: Classical Ehlers-Danlos syndrome is most often caused by pathogenic variants in COL5A1 or COL5A2, which encode type V collagen.
objective: Connect the classical Ehlers-Danlos phenotype with type V collagen gene defects.

sources.title: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes classical EDS as a connective-tissue disorder commonly caused by COL5A1 or COL5A2 variants.

sources.title: COL5A1 gene
sources.support: COL5A1 encodes type V collagen, which helps regulate collagen fibril formation.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Supersaturation of urate leads to deposition of monosodium urate crystals in joints, triggering a neutrophil-rich inflammatory response.
vignette: A 52-year-old man awakens with severe pain, erythema, and swelling of the first metatarsophalangeal joint. Synovial fluid contains needle-shaped crystals with strong negative birefringence.
distractor_notes: Calcium pyrophosphate crystals are rhomboid-shaped and positively birefringent and more often affect knees or wrists.
Septic arthritis can cause an acutely inflamed joint but does not produce negatively birefringent monosodium urate crystals.
Rheumatoid arthritis usually causes chronic symmetric inflammatory polyarthritis rather than abrupt podagra with urate crystals.
Osteoarthritis is a degenerative noninflammatory arthropathy and does not produce crystal-rich synovial fluid.
key_expl: Acute podagra with needle-shaped negatively birefringent crystals is diagnostic of gout.
objective: Diagnose gout by its classic joint distribution and monosodium urate crystal morphology.

sources.title: Gout
sources.support: NIAMS describes gout as inflammatory arthritis caused by urate crystal deposition, often beginning in the great toe.

sources.title: Gout
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes uric acid crystal deposition as the cause of gout and notes sudden painful attacks.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Autoimmune synovial inflammation produces pannus formation, cartilage destruction, and marginal bone erosions, typically in a symmetric small-joint distribution.
vignette: A 43-year-old woman has 4 months of symmetric pain and swelling of the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints with morning stiffness lasting 2 hours. Distal interphalangeal joints are spared.
distractors: Systemic lupus erythematosus without inflammatory arthritis
distractor_notes: Osteoarthritis typically causes brief morning stiffness and frequently involves distal interphalangeal joints with bony enlargement.
Gout usually presents with episodic acute monoarthritis or oligoarthritis rather than persistent symmetric small-joint synovitis.
Psoriatic arthritis often accompanies psoriasis and may involve distal interphalangeal joints, dactylitis, or asymmetric patterns.
Lupus can cause inflammatory arthritis, but the isolated persistent symmetric erosive-type small-joint pattern is more characteristic of rheumatoid arthritis.
key_expl: Prolonged morning stiffness with chronic symmetric MCP/PIP inflammatory arthritis and DIP sparing is classic for rheumatoid arthritis.
objective: Recognize the characteristic distribution and inflammatory stiffness pattern of rheumatoid arthritis.
clues: morning stiffness lasting 2 hours with DIP sparing

sources.title: Rheumatoid Arthritis
sources.support: NIAMS describes rheumatoid arthritis as a chronic autoimmune inflammatory disease that commonly affects joints symmetrically and causes prolonged stiffness.

sources.title: Rheumatoid arthritis
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes symmetric painful swollen joints and morning stiffness as common manifestations of rheumatoid arthritis.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Immune activation involving dendritic cells and the IL-23/Th17 axis promotes keratinocyte hyperproliferation and inflammatory plaque formation.
vignette: A 34-year-old man has sharply demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scale on the elbows and knees and pitting of several fingernails.
lead: Which cellular process most directly accounts for the epidermal thickening in these lesions?
correct: Accelerated keratinocyte proliferation driven by immune cytokine signaling
distractors: Loss of melanocytes from autoimmune destruction
IgG-mediated loss of desmosomal adhesion between keratinocytes
Deposition of monosodium urate in the dermis
Defective type VII collagen anchoring fibrils
distractor_notes: Autoimmune melanocyte loss causes vitiligo, which produces depigmented macules rather than scaly plaques.
Desmoglein autoantibodies cause pemphigus vulgaris with intraepidermal blistering, not psoriatic plaques.
Urate deposition causes tophi and gout rather than widespread epidermal hyperproliferation.
Type VII collagen defects cause dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa with skin fragility and blistering.
key_expl: Psoriasis is an immune-mediated disease in which inflammatory cytokines drive markedly accelerated keratinocyte turnover and plaque formation.
objective: Explain psoriatic plaque formation through immune-driven keratinocyte hyperproliferation.

sources.title: Psoriasis
sources.support: NIAMS describes psoriasis as immune mediated with excessive skin-cell production and inflammation.

sources.title: Psoriasis
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes psoriasis as an immune-related condition causing skin cells to rise too quickly and form thick scaly plaques.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Defects in basal keratin proteins such as keratin 5 or keratin 14 weaken the basal keratinocyte cytoskeleton, causing intraepidermal blistering after minor mechanical trauma.
vignette: A newborn develops recurrent blisters on the hands and feet after minimal friction. Genetic testing identifies a pathogenic KRT14 variant.
lead: Which cellular structure is primarily weakened?
correct: Intermediate filament network of basal keratinocytes
distractors: Type IV collagen in the glomerular basement membrane
Type I collagen fibrils in bone
distractor_notes: Autoantibody-mediated desmosomal disruption causes pemphigus vulgaris, an acquired blistering disease.
Type IV collagen defects produce basement-membrane disorders such as Alport syndrome rather than friction-induced epidermal blistering.
Type I collagen defects cause osteogenesis imperfecta and related connective-tissue phenotypes.
Ciliary microtubule defects cause primary ciliary dyskinesia, not skin fragility.
key_expl: KRT14 encodes keratin 14, an intermediate filament protein in basal keratinocytes; its disruption causes cell fragility in epidermolysis bullosa simplex.
objective: Connect KRT14 defects with failure of basal keratinocyte intermediate filaments and mechanically induced blistering.
clues: blistering after minor friction from birth

sources.title: Epidermolysis bullosa
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes epidermolysis bullosa simplex as a skin-fragility disorder often caused by KRT5 or KRT14 variants.

sources.title: KRT14 gene
sources.support: KRT14 encodes keratin 14, which forms intermediate filaments that provide structural support to basal epidermal cells.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Gain-of-function FGFR3 signaling inhibits chondrocyte proliferation and endochondral ossification, disproportionately limiting growth of long bones.
vignette: A newborn has rhizomelic shortening of the limbs, frontal bossing, and midface hypoplasia. Both parents have average stature.
lead: The pathogenic variant most commonly produces which functional effect?
distractors: Complete loss of type I collagen production
Loss of growth hormone receptor signaling
Constitutive activation of RANKL in osteoblasts
distractor_notes: Type I collagen loss causes osteogenesis imperfecta rather than disproportionate short-limb dwarfism.
Osteoclast acidification defects can cause osteopetrosis, characterized by dense brittle bones.
Growth hormone receptor defects cause proportionate growth failure, not the rhizomelic pattern of achondroplasia.
RANKL activation is not the primary lesion in achondroplasia; the key defect is excessive FGFR3 signaling in growth-plate cartilage.
key_expl: Achondroplasia is caused by activating FGFR3 variants; excessive receptor signaling inhibits endochondral bone growth.
objective: Explain disproportionate short stature in achondroplasia as gain-of-function FGFR3 signaling that suppresses endochondral ossification.

sources.title: Achondroplasia
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes achondroplasia as an FGFR3 gain-of-function skeletal dysplasia affecting endochondral bone growth.

sources.title: FGFR3 gene
sources.support: FGFR3 negatively regulates bone growth; activating variants excessively restrain chondrocyte growth and ossification.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Loss of PTCH1 removes inhibition of Smoothened and constitutively activates Hedgehog signaling, promoting basal cell carcinoma development.
vignette: A 19-year-old man has multiple basal cell carcinomas, jaw keratocysts, and calcification of the falx cerebri. Genetic testing reveals a germline PTCH1 loss-of-function variant.
lead: Which signaling change most directly promotes tumor formation?
correct: Constitutive activation of Hedgehog signaling through Smoothened
distractors: Suppression of beta-catenin degradation by APC gain of function
Loss of RAS activity from excess neurofibromin
Constitutive inhibition of RET tyrosine kinase
distractor_notes: APC loss, not gain of function, increases beta-catenin signaling in familial adenomatous polyposis.
Neurofibromin loss increases RAS signaling; excess neurofibromin would suppress it and is not the mechanism here.
RET activation drives MEN2; inhibition would not explain basal cell nevus syndrome.
Loss of mismatch repair predisposes to Lynch syndrome; increased repair is not oncogenic.
key_expl: PTCH1 normally inhibits Smoothened in the Hedgehog pathway; PTCH1 loss permits constitutive pathway activation and tumor growth.
objective: Connect PTCH1 loss in basal cell nevus syndrome with derepressed Smoothened and Hedgehog signaling.

sources.title: Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes PTCH1-related nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome and its predisposition to multiple basal cell carcinomas.

sources.title: PTCH1 gene
sources.support: PTCH1 encodes Patched-1, a tumor suppressor that restrains Hedgehog signaling by inhibiting Smoothened.
